From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo recap & budget range check — Redwood inference

Hi Alex / Priya — great to meet your team on the call today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size the right Dedicated vs Hosted recommendation: 

1) Volumes: you mentioned ~250M tokens/month for production payments flows plus an additional ~50M tokens for ML batch jobs (fraud scoring prompts) — total ~300M tokens/month. Can you confirm whether the 250M is steady-state or expected to ramp over Q3?

2) Latency profile: 95th percentile target ~300ms for production path; batch jobs are fine with higher latency.

3) Procurement thresholds: you indicated PO required for commitments > $50k/month and legal review for > $150k/month. Please confirm those thresholds and any quarterly/annual billing preferences.

Next steps I propose: once you confirm the volume cadence (steady vs ramp) and procurement thresholds, Dylan and I will put together a budget-range note showing target $/1M tokens for Hosted vs Dedicated, plus recommended rollout (canary -> 100%). Attached: quick forecast template — fill in your month-by-month expected tokens and we’ll produce unit economics back.

Attachments: ZenPay_MonthlyForecast.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Thanks,
Marissa

Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -07:00

Thanks Marissa — quick answers below: 

- Volumes: the 250M tokens/month is our estimated steady-state for production (we expect to hit that in ~8 weeks after launch). The batch 50M is monthly and fairly constant.
- Procurement thresholds: PO required for > $50k/month; anything > $125k/month requires VP procurement sign-off and a 3rd party security attestation (SOC2). Legal review is standard but timelines are usually 2-3 weeks.
- Billing preference: monthly invoicing is fine; if we go to Dedicated we probably want quarterly invoicing.

I attached a slightly edited version of your forecast. Let me know if you need further detail.

Alex

Alex / Marissa — thanks for the clarification. Quick internal note / question for Alex: for a band around 300M tokens/month, our ballpark hosted pricing (with typical batching and prefix caching) would target around $800–$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on model family and temperature. Dedicated unit economics drop that to roughly $350–$700 per 1M tokens once you account for reserved GPU efficiency and pooling across routes. 

To validate procurement: if ZenPay's PO threshold is $50k/month, that translates to roughly 40–60M tokens/month at the hosted upper band. So Dedicated becomes compelling at your scale (~300M) primarily for cost predictability and the procurement simplicity of a committed contract.

Can you confirm the target $/1M tokens you have in mind (or an internal benchmark) so we can tune the proposal? Also any constraints on term length (12 vs 24 months) that procurement prefers?

Cheers,
Dylan
